subject: health
unitTitle: Feelings, Calm, and Asking for Help
title: Explicit model: telling a trusted adult
essentialQuestion: How can I notice what I feel and choose a helpful next step?
materials: paper or cards for a calm-down menu
a card the guardian keeps for trusted-adult contacts
keyPoints: A trusted adult is someone who keeps you safe, listens, and takes action — often a parent, caregiver, teacher, coach, school nurse, or relative.
It helps to have more than one, including one outside your home.
Tell an adult when someone is hurt or unsafe, when something feels wrong, or when a problem is too big to solve alone.
If the first adult does not help, keep telling until someone does.
That is not being a nuisance.
Telling to keep someone safe is never the same as tattling to get someone in trouble.
privacySafeScenario: Priya told one adult that something at the park worried her and was told "do not worry about it." She still feels worried. What should Priya do?
studentTask: The learner applies what they learned about telling a trusted adult to a new fictional situation and records the choice plus the reason behind it.
knowledgeCheck: State the most important rule or fact about telling a trusted adult in your own words.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about telling a trusted adult.
The learner gives a reason, an example, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
adaptationChoices: Calming tools may be movement-based, still, sensory, verbal, or silent, and each learner picks tools their body and setting allow. Any scenario may be answered by pointing, choosing from options, drawing, or speaking.
extensionChallenge: Apply what you learned about telling a trusted adult under a new constraint, compare two reasonable approaches, or teach the idea to a family member with an original fictional example.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, signed, drawn, or pointed responses; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
trustedAdultNote: Direct urgent safety, health, or mental-health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.

optionalReflection.prompt: With a guardian, agree on one calm-down option that is allowed at home and one that is allowed away from home. This is optional. No purchase, account creation, photograph, measurement, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
